Shaak Ti research extraction

Final URL: https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Shaak_Ti/Legends
Continuity label: Legends (the page is the /Legends article and is categorized as a Legends article)
Page warning: Wookieepedia says there are two conflicting sources for this article, Labyrinth of Evil and Star Wars: Clone Wars, and that Lucasfilm has not established a cohesive timeline.

CONCRETE FEATS (article claims with citations)

- Geonosis: Shaak Ti was one of nine Jedi Masters leading the strike team. She fought through hundreds of Techno Union battle droids, boarded a Republic gunship while deflecting blasterfire, then led clone soldiers from the front lines. [14]
- Kamino defense: She oversaw clone-cadet training and administered squad tests. During a Separatist assault, she used the Force to plug a hole in a transparisteel connector bridge and hold the ocean at bay while awaiting rescue. Her strategy later repelled another full-scale assault led by General Grievous and Asajj Ventress. [17][19]
- Hypori: After the Jedi task force was outmaneuvered and surrounded, Shaak Ti used telekinesis to distract General Grievous and held her own against him longer than most of the Jedi; Grievous's revealed second pair of limbs caught her off guard and hurled her into debris. She survived the encounter and was evacuated. [20]
- Brentaal IV: After being shot in the chest by Shogar Tok, she slowed her metabolism so she could heal quickly, then rose and killed Tok during a brief firefight. [5]
- Dagu: She disguised her identity as a Jedi, started a prisoner revolt with clones and enslaved natives, and defeated Count Dooku's Dark Jedi Acolyte Artel Darc, freeing the prisoners. [6]
- Metalorn: After Bail Organa passed her lightsaber into her cell, she freed herself, protected Organa, and escaped the prison facility. [23]
- Coruscant: When a MagnaGuard cut her hand and knocked away her lightsaber, she took an electrostaff and used it as a bo-staff, then recovered her lightsaber and wielded both weapons. She destroyed many MagnaGuards and held them off, but was later too weak to defeat Grievous and was subdued. [24][25]
- Jedi Temple: During Operation: Knightfall, she rallied Jedi, fended off Darth Vader, and organized a mass evacuation of many Initiates, Padawans, Knights, and Masters before escaping herself. [26][27]
- Felucia: In exile, she trained Maris Brood and Force-sensitive Jungle Felucians, became a respected chieftain, commanded multiple tribes, and taught attack/defense uses of the Force in preparation for the Sith. [7][27]
- Felucia duel: She batted aside Starkiller's telekinetic attacks, used the Force to knock him down, called her people to attack him, and commanded the sarlacc's tentacles against him. Starkiller eventually caught her off balance, hit her with Force lightning, and flung her into the air. Mortally injured, she deliberately entered the sarlacc pit. [7]

CITED POWER STATEMENTS AND ASSESSMENTS
(Marked as hype/assessment where the article uses evaluative language rather than documenting an event.)

- Obi-Wan Kenobi: “...and Shaak Ti's the most cunning Jedi I've ever met. She's even taught me a few tricks.” [8] — assessment/character praise.
- Article assessment: She was “a Master of legendary power and strength in the Force” and “among the finest and most cunning swordsmen of her time.” [4] — hype/assessment, not a discrete feat.
- Article assessment: She was “an extremely powerful and accomplished master of the Force and exceptional lightsaber duelist.” [4] — hype/assessment.
- Lightsaber: She was trained in all forms, particularly Makashi and Ataru; the article says her skills were compared to Count Dooku's, and that her swift barrages pressured Galen Marek/Starkiller's Soresu until he had to use the Force. [2][8][29][30][7] — comparison/assessment plus the described duel result.
- Dual weapons: The article credits her improvised Jar'Kai use of a lightsaber and electrostaff with defeating all the MagnaGuards she faced in the Battle of Coruscant. [24] — concrete feat.
- Nature/Felucia: It says her control of fauna and the Consitor Sato technique were potent enough for her to command Felucia's flora and fauna, stop the sarlacc from devouring her, and direct it to attack Marek. [7] — concrete feat as described by the article.
- Telekinesis: The article says Plo Koon praised her mastery; it reports that she moved large objects without hand gestures or looking at them, even while exhausted, threw large objects at high velocity, and deflected Marek's telekinetic assault. [25][7] — concrete feats; “praised” is an assessment.
- Force defenses and other abilities: She held back a Kamino flood, created a barrier that repelled Marek, used Tutaminis to deflect electrostaff blows and repel a glancing lightsaber blow, and concentrated lightning into an attack. [7][31] — concrete feats as described by the article.

DEATH / CONTINUITY NOTES (kept separate)

1) Starkiller — Legends / The Force Unleashed (the article's operative death)
Darth Vader sent his secret apprentice Starkiller to kill Shaak Ti on Felucia. During their duel, Starkiller's Force lightning mortally injured her and flung her from the sarlacc's tentacle; she then purposefully entered the sarlacc pit. The article gives her death as 3 BBY, Felucia, and identifies her last words to Starkiller as: “Poor boy. The Sith always betray one another. But I'm sure you'll learn that soon enough.” [2][7]

2) Grievous — deleted/unused Revenge of the Sith version; non-canon to this Legends account
The article says two Revenge of the Sith death scenes were deleted and Star Wars Insider 87 confirmed neither was canonical; Shaak Ti is alive later in a hologram. In the first version, General Grievous ignited a lightsaber through her heart aboard the Invisible Hand while Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi watched. The article also says this version appeared in storyboards/early screenplay drafts and was completed for the DVD deleted-scenes material. Separately, it says Cartoon Network artists considered having her die at Grievous's hands in the Clone Wars Micro Series to explain her absence. [26][35][36][37]

3) Anakin Skywalker / Darth Vader — deleted Jedi Temple version; non-canon to this Legends account
A second filmed version moved the death to the Jedi Temple during Operation: Knightfall: Vader entered Shaak Ti's room while she meditated and stabbed her in the back. The scene was deleted; the article says she remained alive in the Legends account and was later seen in hologram form. It notes that a similar scene appeared in a vision in The Clone Wars “Voices,” and that current Canon later acknowledged this Vader death, but current Canon is distinct from the Legends account here. [8][26][38][39][41][42]
